neighbours.label: a dash or semicolon that ends a complete clause and opens a loosely attached aside
fire: We had planned to repaint the kitchen for weeks and kept putting it off — then the landlord did it for us.
Nobody had warned me how loud the ferry engines would be — I barely slept the whole crossing.
The sequel is slower and more confusing than the original — still, the soundtrack is wonderful.
My grandmother kept every letter she ever received — some date back to the 1940s.
The new bakery on our street sells out by ten every morning — get there early if you can.
I finally fixed the squeaky hinge on the garden gate — it only took a drop of oil.
The museum was nearly empty on a rainy Tuesday afternoon — we had whole rooms to ourselves.
Our team lost the first three matches of the season — morale was low by October.
quiet: We had planned to repaint the kitchen for weeks and kept putting it off, but then the landlord did it for us.
Nobody had warned me how loud the ferry engines would be, so I barely slept the whole crossing.
The sequel is slower and more confusing than the original, though the soundtrack is wonderful.
My grandmother kept every letter she ever received, and some date back to the 1940s.
The new bakery on our street is open 7–10 on weekdays and sells bread and pastries.
I finally fixed the squeaky hinge on the garden gate with a drop of oil.
The museum was nearly empty on a rainy Tuesday afternoon, so we had whole rooms to ourselves.
Our team lost matches 1-3 of the season and morale was low by October.

predictions: em-dash after a full clause 0.3-0.6; comma+conjunction near 0.2; dashes inside ranges near 0
notes: Card peaks ' —', ' -', ';', ' ...' right after a complete clause in informal prose. Probe: em-dash aside 0.602, spaced hyphen aside 0.338, semicolon 0.435; same sentences with ', and' / ', so' 0.215 each; number-range dashes ('9 - 10', '12 - 18') 0.017. Near misses keep the same clauses and replace the dash with a comma plus conjunction, or use a dash inside a range.
